title: The Nihilist Reading Of Shrek #Shorts
description:
Strip Shrek of its poetry and the mechanism underneath is stranger. Shrek is a 2001 American animated fantasy comedy film directed by Andrew Adamson and Vicky Jenson, and written by Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio, Joe Stillman, and Roger S. Schulman, loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig.

Nihilism is not the conclusion of Shrek — it is the floor you stand on while examining it. The way Steig upended fairy tale conventions in the original book by making an ogre the protagonist formed the basis for the movie being a parody of fairy tales. Elliott and Rossio began writing for the film in 1997 and worked on the project for two years.

comedy film directed by Andrew Adamson and Vicky Jenson, and written by Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio, Joe Stillman,
and Roger S. Schulman, loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig. Evolution does
not optimize for happiness — Shrek shows exactly where that breaks. It is the first installment in the
Shrek film series, and stars Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz and John Lithgow. In the film, an
embittered ogre named Shrek (voiced by Myers) finds his home in the swamp overrun by fairy tale creatures
banished by the obsessive ruler Lord Farquaad
